## REST API interview deep dive

Use this reference when testing or debugging an API: exact status codes, headers, authentication, file uploads, HTTP methods and CORS.

### HTTP status codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **1xx — informational** ||
| 100 | Continue — continue sending the request body |
| 101 | Switching Protocols — protocol switch accepted |
| 102 | Processing — request is still being processed (WebDAV) |
| 103 | Early Hints — preliminary headers before the final response |
| **2xx — successful** ||
| 200 | OK — request succeeded |
| 201 | Created — a resource was created; check Location when applicable |
| 202 | Accepted — accepted for asynchronous processing, not necessarily completed |
| 203 | Non-Authoritative Information — metadata was modified by an intermediary |
| 204 | No Content — success with no response body |
| 205 | Reset Content — client should reset the current view/document |
| 206 | Partial Content — partial representation returned for a Range request |
| 207 | Multi-Status — multiple independent results (WebDAV) |
| 208 | Already Reported — resource already reported in the current response (WebDAV) |
| 226 | IM Used — response represents instance manipulations |
| **3xx — redirection/cache** ||
| 300 | Multiple Choices — multiple possible representations/targets |
| 301 | Moved Permanently — permanent redirect |
| 302 | Found — temporary redirect in common practice |
| 303 | See Other — retrieve another URI, normally with GET |
| 304 | Not Modified — cached representation is still valid |
| 305 | Use Proxy — deprecated |
| 306 | Unused — reserved historical code |
| 307 | Temporary Redirect — preserves method and body |
| 308 | Permanent Redirect — permanent redirect preserving method and body |
| **4xx — client/request problem** ||
| 400 | Bad Request — malformed or invalid request |
| 401 | Unauthorized — authentication is missing or invalid |
| 402 | Payment Required — reserved/payment-specific use |
| 403 | Forbidden — authenticated/known principal is not permitted |
| 404 | Not Found — resource or route not found |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed — method is known but not allowed; inspect Allow |
| 406 | Not Acceptable — content negotiation cannot satisfy Accept |
| 407 | Proxy Authentication Required — proxy requires authentication |
| 408 | Request Timeout — server timed out waiting for the request |
| 409 | Conflict — request conflicts with current resource state |
| 410 | Gone — resource intentionally no longer exists |
| 411 | Length Required — Content-Length is required |
| 412 | Precondition Failed — conditional header such as If-Match failed |
| 413 | Content Too Large — request body/file exceeds a limit |
| 414 | URI Too Long — request target is too long |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type — request media type/body format is unsupported |
| 416 | Range Not Satisfiable — requested byte range cannot be served |
| 417 | Expectation Failed — Expect requirement could not be met |
| 418 | I'm a teapot — historical joke status, not normal business semantics |
| 421 | Misdirected Request — request reached a server unable to answer for the target |
| 422 | Unprocessable Content — syntax is understood but content cannot be processed semantically |
| 423 | Locked — resource is locked (WebDAV) |
| 424 | Failed Dependency — dependent action failed (WebDAV) |
| 425 | Too Early — server rejects a request because replay is considered risky |
| 426 | Upgrade Required — client must switch protocol |
| 428 | Precondition Required — server requires a conditional request |
| 429 | Too Many Requests — rate limit exceeded; inspect Retry-After |
| 431 | Request Header Fields Too Large — request headers are too large |
| 451 | Unavailable For Legal Reasons — access denied for legal reasons |
| **5xx — server/upstream problem** ||
| 500 | Internal Server Error — generic server failure |
| 501 | Not Implemented — requested functionality/method is not implemented |
| 502 | Bad Gateway — gateway/proxy received an invalid upstream response |
| 503 | Service Unavailable — service is temporarily unavailable |
| 504 | Gateway Timeout — gateway/proxy timed out waiting for upstream |
| 505 | HTTP Version Not Supported — HTTP version is unsupported |
| 506 | Variant Also Negotiates — content-negotiation configuration error |
| 507 | Insufficient Storage — server cannot store the representation |
| 508 | Loop Detected — processing loop detected |
| 510 | Not Extended — further extensions are required |
| 511 | Network Authentication Required — client must authenticate to gain network access |

**Interview distinctions:** 401 is primarily an authentication failure; 403 is an authorization/permission failure. 409 is a state conflict; 422 means the server understands the syntax but cannot process the content semantically. 502 and 504 normally involve an upstream dependency through a gateway; 503 means temporarily unavailable.

### HTTP methods

| Method | Purpose | Safe | Idempotent |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GET | Read a representation/resource | Yes | Yes |
| HEAD | GET semantics without response content | Yes | Yes |
| POST | Resource-specific processing; commonly creates a subordinate resource | No | No by definition |
| PUT | Create/replace the state of the target resource | No | Yes |
| PATCH | Apply a partial modification | No | Not guaranteed |
| DELETE | Remove the target resource | No | Yes |
| OPTIONS | Describe communication options; also used for CORS preflight | Yes | Yes |
| CONNECT | Establish a tunnel through a proxy | No | No |
| TRACE | Diagnostic loop-back of the received request | Yes | Yes |

**PUT vs PATCH:** PUT normally expresses the desired complete state of the target resource; PATCH sends partial changes. PATCH may be idempotent if the operation is designed that way, but HTTP does not guarantee it. CRUD is only a useful mapping: Create → commonly POST, Read → GET, Update → PUT/PATCH, Delete → DELETE.

### Useful request headers

- **Accept** — response media types the client can process.
- **Content-Type** — media type of request content, for example application/json or multipart/form-data.
- **Authorization** — Basic/Bearer or another credential carried by HTTP.
- **Cookie** — cookies/session state sent to the server.
- **Origin** — origin initiating a browser cross-origin request; central to CORS.
- **Host** — target host/authority in HTTP/1.1.
- **User-Agent** — client identity/version metadata.
- **Accept-Language / Accept-Encoding** — language and compression negotiation.
- **If-None-Match / If-Match** — ETag-based cache validation and optimistic concurrency.
- **If-Modified-Since / If-Unmodified-Since** — date-based conditional requests.
- **Range** — request only part of a representation.
- **Cache-Control** — request-side cache directives.
- **Referer** — referring page when browser policy permits it.
- **traceparent / correlation IDs** — diagnostics and distributed tracing when supported.

### Useful response headers

- **Content-Type / Content-Encoding / Content-Length** — how to interpret/transfer the body.
- **Location** — created resource URI or redirect target.
- **Set-Cookie** — cookie creation/update; inspect Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain and expiry.
- **Cache-Control / ETag / Last-Modified / Age / Vary** — caching and revalidation.
- **Allow** — allowed methods, especially with 405.
- **WWW-Authenticate** — authentication challenge, especially with 401.
- **Retry-After** — when to retry after responses such as 429 or 503.
- **Content-Disposition** — inline vs attachment and suggested download filename.
- **Access-Control-Allow-Origin / Methods / Headers / Credentials / Expose-Headers** — CORS policy.
- **Server** — server metadata when exposed.
- **API-specific rate-limit headers** — names are not universal; follow the API contract.

### Authentication and authorization for API requests

Authentication answers **who are you?** Authorization answers **what are you allowed to do?**

1. **HTTP Basic** — Authorization: Basic base64(username:password). Base64 is encoding, not encryption; use TLS.
2. **Bearer token** — Authorization: Bearer <token>; token may be opaque or JWT.
3. **API key** — normally a header value; query parameters are more prone to leakage.
4. **OAuth 2.0 access token** — delegated authorization; access tokens are commonly sent as Bearer tokens.
5. **OpenID Connect** — identity layer on OAuth 2.0, commonly used for login/identity.
6. **Session cookie** — server-side or signed session represented by a cookie.
7. **HMAC/request signing** — client signs request components with a secret/private key.
8. **Mutual TLS (mTLS)** — client and server authenticate with certificates.

Test missing, malformed, expired and revoked credentials; wrong audience/scope; valid identity without permission; horizontal/vertical privilege boundaries; token/session expiry and refresh behavior.

### File upload: can a file be sent together with data?

Yes. Common designs:

**Raw binary body** — endpoint expects only the file.

~~~http
POST /documents
Content-Type: application/pdf

<binary PDF bytes>
~~~

application/octet-stream is commonly used for generic binary content.

**multipart/form-data** — file and ordinary fields in one request. Each part has its own headers, so a file can be sent next to text fields or a JSON metadata part.

~~~http
POST /profiles
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...

--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="displayName"

Alice
--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="avatar"; filename="avatar.png"
Content-Type: image/png

<binary PNG bytes>
--boundary--
~~~

**Base64 inside JSON** is possible but increases payload size and processing overhead. Prefer multipart or binary upload unless the contract specifically requires JSON. A scalable alternative is a short-lived pre-signed object-storage URL followed by a separate metadata call.

For file tests cover MIME type, extension vs actual content, zero-byte files, size limit, multiple files, Unicode/duplicate filenames, interrupted upload, integrity/checksum, download Content-Disposition, access control and orphan cleanup.

### CORS: what it is and how it arises

**CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)** is a browser-enforced, HTTP-header-based mechanism that lets a server declare which other origins may make browser script requests and read the response. An origin is **scheme + host + port**. Changing any of those creates a different origin.

Browsers apply the **same-origin policy** to JavaScript. If code loaded from https://app.example.com calls https://api.example.com, the browser treats it as cross-origin. That is why a request can succeed in curl/Postman but fail in browser JavaScript: non-browser clients do not enforce the browser's same-origin policy.

For a request requiring **preflight**, the browser first sends **OPTIONS** with **Origin**, **Access-Control-Request-Method** and possibly **Access-Control-Request-Headers**. The server must answer consistently with headers such as **Access-Control-Allow-Origin**, **Access-Control-Allow-Methods**, **Access-Control-Allow-Headers** and, for credentialed access, **Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true**.

Common CORS failures: missing/wrong Access-Control-Allow-Origin; origin absent from allowlist; OPTIONS returns 404/405/redirect/error; requested method/header is not allowed; credentialed request lacks Access-Control-Allow-Credentials; credentials are combined with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; or a proxy/CDN caches dynamic origin responses without appropriate **Vary: Origin**.

**Important:** CORS is not authentication and does not secure an API against curl, Postman or another server. Real authorization must be enforced by the API itself.

### API debugging checklist

1. Method + URL/path/query/version.
2. Request headers: Content-Type, Accept, auth, cookies, Origin, conditionals.
3. Request body: actual JSON/form/binary structure and encoding.
4. Exact status code, not only the 2xx/4xx class.
5. Response headers: Location, Set-Cookie, cache, auth challenge, Retry-After/rate limit, CORS.
6. Response body and error contract.
7. Timing: DNS/connect/TLS/TTFB/download and upstream delay.
8. Correlation/trace ID for matching server logs/traces.
9. Repeat outside the browser to separate API behavior from CORS/browser behavior.
10. Negative boundaries: auth, wrong method/media type, oversized file, stale ETag, rate limit.

### Sources

- [RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
- [MDN — HTTP response status codes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status)
- [RFC 5789 — PATCH Method for HTTP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789.html)
- [RFC 7578 — multipart/form-data](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7578.html)
- [MDN — Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS)

## REST API — поглиблений блок для співбесід

Практичний довідник для API testing/debugging: точні status codes, headers, authentication, file upload, HTTP methods та CORS.

### HTTP status codes

| Код | Значення |
|---|---|
| **1xx — informational** ||
| 100 | Continue — client може продовжувати надсилати request body |
| 101 | Switching Protocols — server погодив protocol switch |
| 102 | Processing — request ще обробляється (WebDAV) |
| 103 | Early Hints — попередні headers до фінальної відповіді |
| **2xx — successful** ||
| 200 | OK — request успішний |
| 201 | Created — resource створено; за потреби перевіряйте Location |
| 202 | Accepted — прийнято в асинхронну обробку, але ще не обов'язково завершено |
| 203 | Non-Authoritative Information — metadata змінена intermediary |
| 204 | No Content — успіх без response body |
| 205 | Reset Content — client має скинути current view/document |
| 206 | Partial Content — повернено частину representation для Range |
| 207 | Multi-Status — кілька незалежних результатів (WebDAV) |
| 208 | Already Reported — resource вже описаний у response (WebDAV) |
| 226 | IM Used — результат instance manipulations |
| **3xx — redirect/cache** ||
| 300 | Multiple Choices — кілька можливих representations/targets |
| 301 | Moved Permanently — постійний redirect |
| 302 | Found — типовий тимчасовий redirect |
| 303 | See Other — звернутися до іншого URI, зазвичай через GET |
| 304 | Not Modified — cached representation ще актуальний |
| 305 | Use Proxy — deprecated |
| 306 | Unused — reserved historical code |
| 307 | Temporary Redirect — тимчасовий redirect зі збереженням method/body |
| 308 | Permanent Redirect — постійний redirect зі збереженням method/body |
| **4xx — проблема request/client** ||
| 400 | Bad Request — malformed/invalid request |
| 401 | Unauthorized — authentication відсутня або credentials невалідні |
| 402 | Payment Required — reserved/payment-specific |
| 403 | Forbidden — identity відома, але permission недостатньо |
| 404 | Not Found — resource/route не знайдено |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed — method відомий, але тут заборонений; дивіться Allow |
| 406 | Not Acceptable — content negotiation не може задовольнити Accept |
| 407 | Proxy Authentication Required — proxy вимагає authentication |
| 408 | Request Timeout — server не дочекався request |
| 409 | Conflict — request конфліктує з current resource state |
| 410 | Gone — resource навмисно більше не існує |
| 411 | Length Required — потрібен Content-Length |
| 412 | Precondition Failed — conditional header, наприклад If-Match, не виконався |
| 413 | Content Too Large — body/file перевищує limit |
| 414 | URI Too Long — request target завеликий |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type — media type/body format не підтримується |
| 416 | Range Not Satisfiable — requested byte range неможливо віддати |
| 417 | Expectation Failed — вимогу Expect не можна виконати |
| 418 | I'm a teapot — історичний жартівливий code, не business semantics |
| 421 | Misdirected Request — request потрапив на server, який не може відповісти для target |
| 422 | Unprocessable Content — syntax зрозумілий, але content семантично не обробляється |
| 423 | Locked — resource locked (WebDAV) |
| 424 | Failed Dependency — залежна дія впала (WebDAV) |
| 425 | Too Early — server відхиляє request через ризик replay |
| 426 | Upgrade Required — client має перейти на інший protocol |
| 428 | Precondition Required — server вимагає conditional request |
| 429 | Too Many Requests — rate limit exceeded; дивіться Retry-After |
| 431 | Request Header Fields Too Large — request headers завеликі |
| 451 | Unavailable For Legal Reasons — legal restriction |
| **5xx — server/upstream problem** ||
| 500 | Internal Server Error — загальна server failure |
| 501 | Not Implemented — functionality/method не реалізовано |
| 502 | Bad Gateway — gateway/proxy отримав невалідний upstream response |
| 503 | Service Unavailable — сервіс тимчасово unavailable |
| 504 | Gateway Timeout — gateway/proxy не дочекався upstream |
| 505 | HTTP Version Not Supported — HTTP version не підтримується |
| 506 | Variant Also Negotiates — content-negotiation config error |
| 507 | Insufficient Storage — server не може зберегти representation |
| 508 | Loop Detected — processing loop |
| 510 | Not Extended — потрібні додаткові extensions |
| 511 | Network Authentication Required — потрібна authentication для доступу до network |

**Важливі відмінності:** 401 — переважно authentication failure; 403 — authorization/permission failure. 409 — conflict current state; 422 — server розуміє syntax, але не може семантично обробити content. 502/504 зазвичай пов'язані з upstream через gateway, 503 означає тимчасову недоступність.

### HTTP methods

| Method | Призначення | Safe | Idempotent |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GET | Прочитати representation/resource | Так | Так |
| HEAD | GET semantics без response content | Так | Так |
| POST | Resource-specific processing; часто створення subordinate resource | Ні | Ні за визначенням |
| PUT | Створити/повністю замінити state target resource | Ні | Так |
| PATCH | Частково змінити resource | Ні | Не гарантується |
| DELETE | Видалити target resource | Ні | Так |
| OPTIONS | Communication options; також CORS preflight | Так | Так |
| CONNECT | Створити tunnel через proxy | Ні | Ні |
| TRACE | Diagnostic loop-back отриманого request | Так | Так |

**PUT vs PATCH:** PUT зазвичай описує бажаний повний state target resource; PATCH передає часткові зміни. PATCH може бути idempotent, якщо operation так спроєктована, але HTTP цього не гарантує. CRUD — лише корисна відповідність: Create → часто POST, Read → GET, Update → PUT/PATCH, Delete → DELETE.

### Що дивитися в request headers

- **Accept** — які response media types client може обробити.
- **Content-Type** — media type request content: application/json, multipart/form-data тощо.
- **Authorization** — Basic/Bearer або інші HTTP credentials.
- **Cookie** — cookies/session state, що йде server.
- **Origin** — origin browser cross-origin request; ключовий для CORS.
- **Host** — target host/authority для HTTP/1.1.
- **User-Agent** — client/version metadata.
- **Accept-Language / Accept-Encoding** — language/compression negotiation.
- **If-None-Match / If-Match** — ETag, cache validation, optimistic concurrency.
- **If-Modified-Since / If-Unmodified-Since** — date-based conditional requests.
- **Range** — запит частини representation.
- **Cache-Control** — request-side cache directives.
- **Referer** — referring page, коли browser policy дозволяє.
- **traceparent / correlation IDs** — tracing/diagnostics, якщо підтримуються.

### Що дивитися в response headers

- **Content-Type / Content-Encoding / Content-Length** — як інтерпретувати/передавати body.
- **Location** — URI створеного resource або redirect target.
- **Set-Cookie** — cookie; перевіряйте Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, expiry.
- **Cache-Control / ETag / Last-Modified / Age / Vary** — caching/revalidation.
- **Allow** — дозволені methods, особливо при 405.
- **WWW-Authenticate** — authentication challenge, особливо при 401.
- **Retry-After** — коли retry після 429/503.
- **Content-Disposition** — inline/attachment і filename для download.
- **Access-Control-Allow-Origin / Methods / Headers / Credentials / Expose-Headers** — CORS policy.
- **Server** — server metadata, якщо її не приховано.
- **API-specific rate-limit headers** — names не універсальні; дивіться API contract.

### Методи authentication/authorization для API request

Authentication = **хто ти?** Authorization = **що тобі дозволено?**

1. **HTTP Basic** — Authorization: Basic base64(username:password). Base64 не encryption; потрібен TLS.
2. **Bearer token** — Authorization: Bearer <token>; token може бути opaque або JWT.
3. **API key** — зазвичай header; query parameter легше витікає в logs/history.
4. **OAuth 2.0 access token** — delegated authorization; access token часто йде як Bearer.
5. **OpenID Connect** — identity layer поверх OAuth 2.0; типовий login/identity use case.
6. **Session cookie** — server-side/signed session у cookie.
7. **HMAC/request signing** — request components підписуються secret/private key.
8. **Mutual TLS (mTLS)** — client і server автентифікуються certificates.

Перевіряйте missing/malformed/expired/revoked credentials, wrong audience/scope, valid identity без permission, horizontal/vertical privilege boundaries, token/session expiry та refresh.

### Як передати файл і чи можна разом з іншими даними?

Так.

**Raw binary body** — endpoint очікує тільки файл.

~~~http
POST /documents
Content-Type: application/pdf

<binary PDF bytes>
~~~

Для generic binary content часто використовують application/octet-stream.

**multipart/form-data** — файл і звичайні поля в одному request. Кожен part має власні headers, тому поряд із file можна передати text fields або окремий JSON metadata part.

~~~http
POST /profiles
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...

--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="displayName"

Alice
--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="avatar"; filename="avatar.png"
Content-Type: image/png

<binary PNG bytes>
--boundary--
~~~

**Base64 у JSON** технічно можливий, але збільшує payload та processing overhead. Зазвичай краще multipart/binary upload. Ще одна типова схема: короткоживий pre-signed object-storage URL → direct upload → окреме збереження metadata.

Для file testing перевіряйте MIME type, extension vs actual content, zero-byte, max size, multiple files, Unicode/duplicate filenames, interrupted upload, checksum/integrity, Content-Disposition при download, access control та orphan cleanup.

### CORS: що це і як виникає

**CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)** — browser-enforced механізм на HTTP headers, через який server визначає, яким іншим origins browser JavaScript може робити requests і читати response. **Origin = scheme + host + port**; зміна будь-якої частини означає інший origin.

Browser застосовує **same-origin policy** до JavaScript. Якщо code з https://app.example.com викликає https://api.example.com, request cross-origin. Тому API може працювати в curl/Postman, але давати CORS error у browser: curl/Postman не enforce browser same-origin policy.

Коли потрібен **preflight**, browser спочатку надсилає **OPTIONS** з **Origin**, **Access-Control-Request-Method** і, за потреби, **Access-Control-Request-Headers**. Server відповідає через **Access-Control-Allow-Origin**, **Access-Control-Allow-Methods**, **Access-Control-Allow-Headers** та, для credentials, **Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true**.

Типові CORS failures: відсутній/неправильний Access-Control-Allow-Origin; origin не в allowlist; OPTIONS повертає 404/405/redirect/error; method/header не дозволено; для credentialed request немає Access-Control-Allow-Credentials; credentials поєднані з Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; proxy/CDN кешує dynamic origin response без правильного **Vary: Origin**.

**Важливо:** CORS — не authentication і не захист API від curl/Postman/інших серверів. Реальна authorization завжди має enforce-итись самим API.

### API debugging checklist

1. Method + URL/path/query/version.
2. Request headers: Content-Type, Accept, auth, cookies, Origin, conditionals.
3. Request body: реальна JSON/form/binary структура та encoding.
4. Точний status code, а не тільки class 2xx/4xx.
5. Response headers: Location, Set-Cookie, cache, auth challenge, Retry-After/rate limit, CORS.
6. Response body/error contract.
7. Timing: DNS/connect/TLS/TTFB/download/upstream delay.
8. Correlation/trace ID для server logs/traces.
9. Повторити поза browser, щоб відділити API behavior від CORS/browser behavior.
10. Negative boundaries: auth, wrong method/media type, oversized file, stale ETag, rate limit.

### Sources

- [RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
- [MDN — HTTP response status codes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status)
- [RFC 5789 — PATCH Method for HTTP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789.html)
- [RFC 7578 — multipart/form-data](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7578.html)
- [MDN — Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS)
